subject: Measuring duration and pauses between very short signals with timer function

messages.author: fe1cd1573520a129
messages.subject: Measuring duration and pauses between very short signals with timer function
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am trying to measure the duration of the notes of a call and the pauses between the notes (spectrogram attached). However, the notes are very short (0.001-0.003 s) and the amplitude of the notes raises throughout the call. It is really difficult to segregate the signal from the noise, because the inicial notes have small amplitudes. I thought maybe a good solution would be to  restrict the frequency or to use the length of the pauses to try to target only the signal, but neither are possible with timer function. I am using the following parameters:

temp_param <- timer (som, f = 44100, threshold = 5, dmin=0.001, msmooth = c(64,75))

Any ideas? Thank you very much!


Me. Pedro P. G. Taucce

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Measuring duration and pauses between very short signals with timer function
parts:
Hello Pedro,

Your question converges with the one posted by Page. I will really try to add a pause duration argument, but please be patient as I never know how much I can save for seewave.
Regarding the frequency selection, you should apply a fir() filter first, something like:

som.filt <- fir(som, from=2000, to=4000, output="Wave")

fir() is currently slow but will be fast in the next version of seewave (same remark as above: will be realeased soon but time is missing...)

Jerome
